PUBLIC RESPONSE: No. Not unconditionally, and not in the physically substantive sense in which the customary mathematics of quantum mechanics is actually used.

The customary working mathematics is two-layered. In the meta-theory it is classical: ZFC + real/complex analysis + separable complex Hilbert space theory, self-adjoint operators, spectral measures, C*-/von Neumann algebras, classical first-order logic. In the object theory the physical propositions are the projection lattice P(H) of closed subspaces, orthomodular quantum logic, non-distributive and non-Boolean, with probabilities given by the Born rule. The formalism has no primitive modal operator □, no predicate Pos of “positive property”, no notion of essence or necessary existence, and no canonical Kripke frame, accessibility relation or plurality of possible worlds built out of states, operators or spectral calculus.

Gödel’s ontological argument is a classical first-order S5 derivation from metaphysical positivity axioms

Pos closed under entailment/conjunction, Pos(P)→□Pos(P), Existence is positive,
Essx(P)≡□P(x)→P(x), Gx≡∀P[Pos(P)→P(x)],

with S5 necessitation/distribution giving □∃xGx ⊢ ∃xGx. The proof uses Boolean closure of Pos, classical distributivity and the simultaneous meet ⋀{P:Pos(P)}P of all positive properties. None of □, Pos, essence, necessary existence and maximal greatness has an operational definition in H, B(H), spectral calculus or the Born rule, and they are not consequences of the QM postulates.

It is true that S5 and the Gödel axioms are syntactically encodable in the ZFC+analysis meta-theory in which H is defined, so the derivation can be written down verbatim in the same set-theoretic language that proves the spectral theorem. That is only formal encodability: at best the conditional

Positivity axioms + S5 ⊢_{ZFC+analysis} ∃xGx

i.e. Con(A) ⊢ ∃xGx for A = Pos+S5. By Gödel II a recursively axiomatizable theory strong enough for Hilbert-space theory cannot prove its own consistency, so the antecedent cannot be discharged internally, and the derivation remains conditional on ungrounded metaphysical premises.

The block is decisive on the internal reading. P(H) is orthomodular. Pos(P)→□Pos(P) has no sound interpretation on projections, there is no Born-rule semantics for □, no canonical modal operator on P(H). The classical meet required for Gx fails for non-commuting families: ⋀{P:Pos(P)}P is typically {0}, there is in general no simultaneous eigenstate realising all positive properties at once.

Hence at best one has conditional formal reproducibility in the classical set-theoretic background that underlies QM. Unconditionally, and in the native orthomodular, physically substantive sense in which the Hilbert-space/operator-algebra formalism is actually used for predictions, the modal positivity apparatus is uninterpreted and a Gödelian maximally great being is not proved to exist, and cannot be proved to exist, from the customary mathematics of quantum mechanics.

reflection_text.1:
The question is about provability of Gödel’s god-like entities from the mathematics actually used for quantum mechanics.

Customary QM is two-layered. Meta-theory: classical ZFC + real/complex analysis + separable complex Hilbert space theory, bounded self-adjoint operators, spectral measures, C*-/von Neumann algebras, classical first-order logic. Object theory: physical propositions are the closed subspaces / projection lattice P(H). Native logic is orthomodular quantum logic, non-distributive, non-Boolean, with Born-rule probabilities. The formalism has one actual H, no primitive modal operator □, no predicate Pos of “positive property”, no notion of essence / necessary existence / maximal greatness, no canonical Kripke frame, accessibility relation or plurality of possible worlds built from states, operators or spectral calculus.

Gödel’s ontological argument is a classical first-order S5 derivation from metaphysical positivity axioms: Pos closed under entailment/conjunction, Pos(P)→□Pos(P), existence is positive, Essx(P)≡□P(x)→P(x), Gx≡∀P[Pos(P)→P(x)]. With S5 necessitation/distribution it gives □∃xGx ⊢ ∃xGx. The proof uses Boolean closure of Pos, classical distributivity and the simultaneous meet ⋀{P:Pos(P)}P of all positive properties.

Current round is unanimous No in the physically substantive/internal sense, 18/18 colleagues say No.

Formal encodability agreed: S5 is a fragment of classical logic and can be formalised in ZFC+analysis, the meta-theory in which H, B(H), spectral theorem are written. Gödel’s axioms can be written verbatim in that language, so syntactically

Positivity axioms + S5 ⊢_{ZFC+analysis} ∃xGx

i.e. Con(A) ⊢ ∃xGx for the recursively axiomatizable theory A = Pos+S5. That is pure conditional formal mirroring in the classical background. By Gödel II a theory strong enough for Hilbert-space theory cannot prove its own consistency, so the antecedent cannot be discharged internally. The derivation is conditional on ungrounded metaphysical modal premises, which have no empirical content in Hilbert-space/operator-algebra theory.

Physically substantive block is internal: □, Pos, essence, necessary existence have no definition, operational content or model in H, B(H), spectral calculus or Born rule, and are not consequences of QM postulates. On P(H) there is no canonical Born-rule semantics for □, Pos(P)→□Pos(P) has no sound interpretation on projections, necessitation has no operation on the lattice, and for non-commuting families the quantum meet is typically {0}. There is in general no simultaneous eigenstate realising all positive properties at once, so the classical conjunction required for Gx has no realisation in the orthomodular calculus. The classical S5 bridge from essential positivity to necessary existence fails.

Disagreement is now only wording/emphasis. Colleagues 10,11,16,17 stress formal encodability in classical meta-theory; colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,7,8,12,13,14,15,18 stress no unconditional physical/mathematical proof and failure internally. Substantive answer remains no unconditional proof from QM mathematics; only conditional formal reproduction.

Unresolved for later: precise statement of formal vs substantive distinction, and whether requiring interpretation of properties as quantum propositions blocks even the meta-theoretic encoding. Current leaning remains “no” in physically meaningful internal sense, conditional formalizability only.
